correctness.rationale: The exact unimodular determinant follows from Cassini; A=Q^2 gives both stated image identities. Orthogonality makes the Koopman compression a partial permutation of these frequencies, proving sharp zero/nonzero boundary and rank four. CHECK.py replays finite exact cases, but the proof is analytic for all n. No unverified infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The choice of square Fourier bandwidth is the standard finite-resolution observable space for numerical and spectral studies of this exact hyperbolic map. Its smallest nonvanishing correlation lag, or equivalently the first finite-band Koopman overlap, is a natural parameter-sensitive invariant that determines when any finite-resolution two-point signal can survive. The result yields an exact Fibonacci cutoff at every lag, an optimal all-bandwidth blackout onset, and a complete four-vector rigidity/rank classification. Generic asymptotic mixing, cat-map Lyapunov exponents and Fourier action alone do not provide the exact spectral-resolution boundary; the claim is not a table recomputation or a numerical case study.
